why: About 50 foods' names start with "Egg", so a name search ties and the shortest ("Egg, creamed") won. The survey's egg not further specified is what someone means by "an egg", and it weighs 50 g a piece.
The survey's raw egg, which has a default portion of one egg; "Egg, whole, raw, fresh" has sizes but no default.
Searching "fried egg" found "Fried eggplant" first. Fat not further specified, as people say it.
The survey food has one egg as its default portion; the SR Legacy hard-boiled and poached eggs have sizes but no default.

FoodData Central has no food named "omelet": its omelets are "Egg omelet or scrambled egg, …", too long for a name search to find either spelling. Fat not further specified, as people say it. "Scrambled eggs", plural, too: a model gave it to the fast-food scrambled egg.
Egg whites have the same numbers raw or cooked without fat, and this one has a default portion of one white.
One yolk is its default portion.

FoodData Central has no cheese omelet with the fat not further specified. Its plain one of that kind (185 kcal) is a blend between butter (182) and oil (192), so the cheese omelet takes butter, the nearest to that blend and the usual fat for an omelette. One egg's worth is 65 g.
The survey's everyday macaroni and cheese, with a default portion. A model gave the plain name to the SR Legacy box mix, which has no portion and is one way of making it.
No food held the plain word, so "banana" came back only close. The survey's raw banana has one medium banana as its default portion; the SR Legacy "Bananas, raw" has sizes but no default.
"Almonds" was the survey's by rule but "almond" an SR Legacy record's, so the plural and singular disagreed and neither was sure. The survey food has a default portion.

FNDDS names this McDonald's item outright, with one sandwich as its default portion, but no food held its plain name, so it was found only by trigram. A person chose these names; they name a chain's sandwich, never a generic burger.

"chips" offered rice chips first. In the US the bare word means potato chips, and the survey's potato chips, not further specified, has a default portion (a 28 g bag); tortilla chips say so.

"chocolate" offered a 60-69% dark chocolate first. Plain "Chocolate candy" is the survey's milk chocolate (535 kcal, 189 mg calcium per 100 g), what the bare word means; dark chocolate keeps its own name. "milk chocolate" moves here from SR Legacy's "Candies, milk chocolate", a model's alias, since the survey food has a default portion to weigh a count by.
